newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales light at $65-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales light at $65-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales early Wednesday were light at $65.00 per cwt, steady with late activity on Tuesday and down $1.00 from last week's top, feedlot sources said.
About 5,000 head sold early Wednesday in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area following about 11,000 late Tuesday in that area, they said.
However, some bids at $64.00 were passed by owners pricing cattle mostly at $66.00, with a few at $67.00, sources said.
An estimated 16,000 head sold Tuesday in Kansas, with no early sales reported Wednesday, cattle feeders there said.
Cattle owners reportedly were reluctant to sell below $65.00 because most would see profits vanish at that price, several feedlot sources said.
"At $65.00 a few are making money, but no one will be making money at $64.00," one Kansas feedlot source said.
Declines in fed cattle prices were attributed to a steep drop in boxed beef prices on Tuesday and ideas last week's strong gains in cattle and beef was overdone, sources said.
Weakness also was tied to increased supplies of fed cattle this week, along with greater numbers of formulated and contract cattle available to packers since August 1.
